newsitem.title: USA: Sears says retail business strong.
newsitem.headline: Sears says retail business strong.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co said Thursday earnings were lower in the second quarter because of a legal settlement with credit card customers, but its retail business was strong despite cool spring weather.

"We want to focus on the impressive underlying performance of our business, which benefited from a shift in the balance of sale to higher-margin apparel merchandise, improved logistics costs and savings realized from merchandise sourcing initiatives," Sears chairman and chief executive Arthur Martinez said in a statement.
Earlier Sears said it earned $117 million or $0.29 a share in the second quarter compared to $274 million or $0.67 in the same period a year ago. Revenues rose 6.6 percent to $9.73 billion.

The results included a charge of $320 million to cover estimated costs to settle claims that Sears was too aggressive in handling repayment agreements with credit card customers who had filed for bankruptcy. Sears also recorded gains of $35 million for an accounting change and $91 million for the sale of its 30-percent stake in data services business Advantis.

Excluding those items, second-quarter net income rose to $311 million, or $0.78 a share, from $274 million, or $0.67 a share, in the second quarter of 1996, Sears said. Wall Street analysts had expected earnings of $0.74 a share in the second quarter of this year, according to First Call.

"In our full-line stores, softlines sales continued to expand during the quarter, especially women's apparel, footwear, fine jewelry and cosmetics and fragrances. Although cooler than normal weather slowed the purchases of air conditioners and lawn and garden equipment, hardlines sales rebounded in June," Martinez said.

Operating income from domestic operations was $92 million for the second quarter compared to $461 million in the same period last year. Excluding the impact of the one-time items, domestic operating income was $509 million for the quarter of 1997. Revenues for domestic operations were $8.94 billion, a 7.1 percent increase, driven by a same-store sales gain of 2.3 percent, 300 new stores and higher credit revenues.

Domestic gross margins as a percentage of merchandise sales and services rose to 26.7 percent from 26.4 percent a year ago. Selling and administrative expense as a percentage of revenues improved to 20.4 percent from 21.3 percent.

Credit revenues rose by 11 percent due to higher receivable balance driven by strong merchandise sales, partially offset by the effects of the accounting change. The domestic provision for uncollectible accounts was $308 million, a 20.9 percent increase a year ago.

International operations include only Sears' interest in Sears Canada as a result of the sale of the company's controlling interest in Sears Mexico during the first quarter. International operations posted second-quarter income of $4 million, compared with a loss of $14 million a year ago.
